entities.title: No leap-second table
entities.summary: The library ships no leap-second table, so it cannot place second 60 or add SI seconds to a POSIX instant.
entities.impact: Second 60 is unsupported (leap-second) when parsing, constructing or resolving; Instant.Add(ElapsedSeconds) and adding an elapsed amount are always unsupported (needs-leap-seconds).
entities.workaround: Use POSIX seconds (PosixSeconds, clock-ticks amounts), which are exact on a POSIX instant.

entities.title: POSIX instants given as ticks only
entities.summary: Instants are read only in the utv.timescale unix-posix version 1 timescale, and only as ticks with an optional subTick.
entities.impact: Instants in other timescales (TAI, UTC with leap seconds, GPS, …) or given as a coordinate are unsupported (unsupported-operand) in every everyday operation.

entities.title: Proleptic Gregorian only
entities.summary: Civil operations and semantic validation work only on calendar gregory with chronology proleptic.
entities.impact: Any other calendar or chronology is unsupported (unsupported-calendar), from GregorianCivil.Validate and from every everyday operation.

entities.title: Five resolution policies are not implemented
entities.summary: Of the schema's resolution policies, gap shift-backward-by-gap, next-valid-boundary and previous-valid-boundary, and overlap offset-match and occurrence-index, are not implemented.
entities.impact: Resolving with any of them is unsupported (unsupported-policy).
entities.workaround: An offsetAssertion on the value selects a side of an overlap.

entities.title: Start-end intervals of dates or instants only
entities.summary: Contains and Overlaps work on intervals whose domain is civil/gregory (dates) or physical (POSIX instants), built start-end.
entities.impact: Other domains, start-amount and amount-end intervals, and date-time points are unsupported (unsupported-operand).

entities.title: ISO 8601 extended format only
entities.summary: parseIso and parseText read the extended format of ISO 8601 and RFC 3339 / RFC 9557, with at most nine fraction digits.
entities.impact: Week dates, ordinal dates, basic format, a year alone, a decimal comma, times with T or an offset, 24:00 and EDTF qualifiers are unsupported; more than nine fraction digits is unsupported (implementation-limit).

entities.title: .NET's own range
entities.summary: Conversions back to .NET are limited by what the .NET types hold.
entities.impact: Years outside 1..9999, nanoseconds that are not a multiple of 100, offsets that are not whole minutes or beyond ±14:00, and amounts beyond TimeSpan give unsupported (out-of-native-range). A DateTime cannot hold a zone or offset; a calendar period has no TimeSpan.

entities.title: JSON-layer builders take 64-bit numbers
entities.summary: Build.Date, Build.YearMonth, Build.DateTime, Build.Instant and Build.Period take long arguments.
entities.impact: A year or component beyond a long cannot be built with Build; the operations still accept such values as JSON, and CivilDate.Of takes a BigInteger year.
entities.workaround: Write the JSON directly, or use the typed constructors.

entities.title: A failed oneOf reports only itself
entities.summary: When a value fails a oneOf in the schema (for example an interval bound holding a bad nested value), only a schema-violation at the oneOf's location is reported.
entities.impact: The diagnostic does not say which part of the nested value is wrong.
